title: Focus Gain sprint log — metrics & micro-experiments
content:
Week window: 2026-03-02 -> 2026-03-08

Quick summary:
- Objective: ship momentum on two small, high-leverage items while protecting 8+ hours of deep work per week.
- Outcome: shipped rollout toggle for fast-path caching (PR merged), ran 2 evaluation batches (one failed regression), lost 3 hours to unplanned meetings.

Quantitative checkpoints (target vs actual):
- PRs merged: target 3, actual 1 (blocked by review queue)
- Evals executed: target 2, actual 2 (1 regression found)
- Deep-focus hours preserved: target 8, actual 5
- Interruptions (meetings + context switches): target <=4, actual 7

Micro-experiments (what I tried):
1) Time-block morning 9:00-12:00 for no-meeting coding (hypothesis: increases PR throughput). Result: protected blocks happened 3/5 days, high productivity on Wed/Thu, but calls bled into Friday block. Learn: escalate calendar boundaries to manager; set Slack status + brief note in team channel.
2) Pull-request pre-review checklist on my side (reduce reviewer back-and-forth). Result: marginally fewer comments on small PRs but larger infra PR still had architectural questions. Next: add brief diagram to PRs >200 LOC.
3) Quick eval smoke-run before full regression (hypothesis: catches obvious issues earlier). Result: prevented a larger rerun; found a tokenizer edge-case. Keep this.

Retrospective notes (questions + blockers):
- Why did deep work drop? Mostly because of 2 ad-hoc customer syncs and a priority pivot email thread. Action: propose a standing biweekly 30-min customer catch-up slot for Solutions ENG to concentrate context.
- Review latency soared because of team review overload. Action: rotate a dedicated reviewer for infra items; pair on first pass.
- Regression root cause: tokenization differences between v0.9 and v1.0 quantized model build. Next step: file small repro, assign to Nikolai, add to regression test matrix.

Actions for next sprint (week of 2026-03-09):
- A1: Protect 10 morning hours (block recurring calendar) and notify manager — owner: me — due: 2026-03-09
- A2: Add diagram template to PR description for >200 LOC — owner: me — due: 2026-03-11
- A3: Create a 5-step eval smoke checklist and add to repo docs — owner: me + Sam Cho — due: 2026-03-12
- A4: Create a short Confluence note summarizing the tokenizer regression + repro steps — owner: me — due: 2026-03-10

Success criteria for the sprint:
- PR merge rate improves to >=2
- One regression prevented by smoke-run
- Deep-focus hours >=8

Signal tracker (for quick check each day):
- Morning block status: green/yellow/red
- Number of context switches >3: yes/no
- Quick eval run done: yes/no

Notes to self (loose/thinking):
- When an infra PR requires architecture-level review, include a short "decision-needed" section with options + tradeoffs (reduces back-and-forth).
- Keep experiments small (1-week cycles) and measure one metric only.
- Share wins with team in Friday sync to reinforce behavior (time-blocking + pre-review checklist).

Linked references and quick links:
- Confluence notes: CONFLUENCE-ENG-4321 (Personal sprint playbook)
- Blocking ticket: JIRA-ENG-998
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/431

Open questions (for 1:1 with manager):
- Can we reduce recurring cross-team sync cadence?
- Opportunity to test a dedicated reviewer rotation pilot for infra items?

End of sprint log.

Timestamp: 2026-03-10 18:12 — last quick edit: added action owners and due dates.
